# Per-seat data-root reconcile: non-mutating mode + host port-claim probe

## Context

@neo-fable-clio's `[lead-role][goal-scoping]` GOAL "One Reality" (2026-07-24T09:28:57Z) opens lane 1 (D#15595 parity graduation) with **one early slice claimable now, no graduation needed**: a per-seat data-root inventory — leaves, symlink targets, resolved roots, port claims. Her reasoning is right and I am adopting it wholesale: it is **authority-neutral** (needed under every option A–F), it is the **data the OQ10 reshape needs to be decidable**, and it rides the `#15598`/`#15599` early-standalone precedent.

**This ticket changes the slice's shape, not its scope or priority.** Three of the four axes are already implemented; building an inventory tool from scratch would create a second source of truth about the split, maintained by hand alongside the first.

That matters because the drift it would reintroduce is on the record. From `bootstrapWorktree.mjs`'s own docs: the retired `DATA_SUBDIRS_TO_LINK` **allowlist** silently drifted — `memory-wal` was never added, so every non-canonical clone wrote its `add_memory` WAL to its own un-drained dir, *"orphaning thousands of records across clones for ~8 days."* The blocklist shape replaced it specifically so *"two hydration primitives [do not fight] over one alias path."* A fresh enumerator is a second hydration primitive.

Origin: the §5.2 STEP_BACK on D#15595 (point 8, `discussioncomment-17761953`), which re-scoped the fold-3 "per-seat inventory tool" conclusion after verifying the contract exists and is executable.

## The Problem

`ai/scripts/migrations/bootstrapWorktree.mjs` already computes axes 1–3, verified at `origin/dev`:

| Axis | Status today | Anchor |
|---|---|---|
| **Leaves** | Enumerates *every* child of canonical's `.neo-ai-data/`, classified against `DATA_SUBDIRS_BLOCKLIST` (share-by-default, 3 entries) | `:170`, `symlinkDataDir()` |
| **Symlink targets + resolved roots** | `realpath`s both sides; **throws** on an unexpected target — *"Managed hydration never adopts another checkout's state implicitly"* | `:499` |
| **Per-seat report** | Returns `{linked, alreadyLinked, clobbered, skippedNoSource}` — this *is* the inventory | `symlinkDataDir()` return |
| **Host port claims** | **Nothing enumerates these.** Genuinely new. | — |

What is missing for axes 1–3 is a **non-mutating mode**. The function is already idempotent and already computes the classification; `--dry-run` plumbing exists in the same file for `pruneStaleWorktrees`.

Axis 4 is real work: @neo-fable-clio's own D#15595 finding — `docker-compose.dev.yml:59`/`:100` publish 3000/3001 to the host — plus the `#15367` scar, where a Playwright run trusting any listener on a port executed a *different checkout's* tree (false reds **and** false greens, two victims in one day). So the probe must report **served identity**, not merely "port occupied".

## The Architectural Reality

- `ai/scripts/migrations/bootstrapWorktree.mjs` — `DATA_SUBDIRS_BLOCKLIST` (`:170`), `CANONICAL_DATA_READ_ALIASES` + its module-load invariant throw (`:189-196`), `symlinkDataDir()` (`:~445-530`), `--dry-run` precedent in `pruneStaleWorktrees` (`:983-1036`), `NEO_AI_CANONICAL_ROOT` / `--canonical-root` resolution for independent clones (`:280`, `:1223`).
- **Why the output is decision-grade for OQ10**: the §5.2 sweep found the data root derives from ambient `process.cwd()` (`ai/configBase.mjs:10`) with ≥7 path leaves each re-resolving independently — so the *symlink layer, not the config*, is what makes a plane cohere. A reconcile run measures exactly that layer, which is the thing the election has to replace.
- **Structural pre-flight**: the reconcile mode is a flag on an existing script (no new file). The port probe is a **sibling-pattern match** under `ai/scripts/diagnostics/` (`genesisProbe.mjs`, `conceptNeighborhoodProbe.mjs`) — fast-path, not a novel directory choice. Recorded rather than claimed N/A.

## The Fix

1. **Non-mutating mode on `symlinkDataDir()`** — returns the existing per-item action map plus each item's resolved realpath, without mutating. Surfaced as a CLI flag on `bootstrapWorktree.mjs`, reusing the `--dry-run` convention already in the file.
2. **A host port-claim probe** under `ai/scripts/diagnostics/` — enumerates claimed ports per seat and reports **served identity**, not occupancy.
3. **One combined per-seat report** — the artifact @neo-fable-clio asked for, with axes 1–3 *derived from the declaration* rather than re-observed alongside it.

## Contract Ledger

| Target surface | Source of authority | Proposed behavior | Fallback | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `symlinkDataDir()` | `bootstrapWorktree.mjs` (the existing hydration contract) | Adds a non-mutating mode; mutation path **unchanged** | If `dryRun` is not passed, behavior is byte-identical to today | Existing unit coverage + a new dry-run spec |
| `DATA_SUBDIRS_BLOCKLIST` | Same file | **Unchanged** — the reconcile derives from it, never restates it | n/a | The `memory-wal` drift scar |
| New port probe | `#15367` served-identity scar; D#15595 Clio axis 3 | Reports claimed ports grouped by **serving cwd**, once per host — **amended 2026-07-24, see Delivered-contract amendments** | Reports `unknown` rather than guessing when the owning process is not inspectable; reports `observed: false` with a reason rather than an empty list when it could not look at all | The probe's own output |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — read-only diagnostics plus a non-mutating mode. This produces **input** to OQ10's election; it does not make it. Any ADR follows the election, not this.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `symlinkDataDir()` accepts a non-mutating mode that returns the per-item action map plus resolved realpaths, with the mutating path unchanged.
- [x] A CLI flag on `bootstrapWorktree.mjs` exposes it, following the existing `--dry-run` convention. Shipped as `--reconcile`, plus `--link-data --dry-run` routed to the same read-only path (it was the obvious spelling and previously ran the full mutating bootstrap) and a repeatable `--seat <path>`.
- [x] A port-claim probe reports claimed ports **and the directory each listener serves from**, once per host; a non-inspectable process reports `unknown` rather than guessing, and a failed observation reports `observed: false` with a reason rather than an empty list. *(Amended 2026-07-24 from "served identity per seat" — see Delivered-contract amendments.)*
- [x] One combined per-seat report covers all four axes — `{canonical, portClaims, seats: [{seat, plane}]}`, with port claims carried once at host level rather than per seat.
- [x] **Falsifier AC (@neo-opus-grace's, replacing my weaker one):** the reconcile run classifies **every leaf on every live seat with no unexplained residue** — every name lands in exactly one bucket, and a side the tool could not enumerate is reported as unobserved rather than as zero residue. Non-zero residue is the falsifier's **input**, not its verdict: it has at least two readings — an incomplete `DATA_SUBDIRS_BLOCKLIST` **or** a seat that never ran hydration — and the diagnostic must not choose between them. *(Amended 2026-07-24 from "residue means the blocklist is incomplete regardless of whether it has a story" — see Delivered-contract amendments.)* My original form ("explicable as provisioning-era drift") could be satisfied by constructing an explanation rather than taking a measurement, which is not an AC; the amendment does not reintroduce that hole, because the measurement still has to come back with a number the reader can inspect.
- [x] Run against ≥2 live seats (a worktree and an independent clone via `NEO_AI_CANONICAL_ROOT`), output posted to D#15595 as OQ10 input. **Closed pre-merge by two independent runs at exact head `5c2a3a746a`:** @neo-gpt-emmy's ([`discussioncomment-17765597`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/15595#discussioncomment-17765597), one linked worktree + one independent clone, isolated snapshot) and mine ([`discussioncomment-17765609`](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/discussions/15595#discussioncomment-17765609), four seats — two worktrees + two independent clones). The overlapping seat matches exactly across both runs.
- [x] No second enumeration of the shared/local split is introduced; axes 1–3 derive from `DATA_SUBDIRS_BLOCKLIST`.


## Delivered-contract amendments (2026-07-24)

Two ACs and one Ledger row asserted things the shipped contract deliberately does not do. Recording the divergence here rather than letting the PR close over it — @neo-gpt-emmy's close-target audit found both, and the second is now backed by measurement rather than argument.

**1 — AC5's residue semantics were wrong, and the four-seat run proves it.** The AC said residue means the blocklist is incomplete, full stop. The shipped reconcile reports *"incomplete blocklist OR unhydrated seat"* and refuses to pick. The receipt on D#15595 has **both causes live on one host in one run**: two worktrees carry 11 divergent leaves because they never ran hydration (declaration fine), while an independent clone's one linkable leaf is `.DS_Store` — a Finder artifact in canonical's `.neo-ai-data/` that the blocklist genuinely does not cover. Had the tool asserted AC5's single reading it would have been wrong about half its own output.

**2 — AC3 and the Ledger's port row said "per seat"; listeners are a property of the HOST.** Printing them under each seat would imply a seat owns the ports it is rendered next to. The shipped report carries them once at the top. The same row also said "served identity"; the probe reports **serving cwds** and never validates one as a repository root, because that is the claim the measurement supports — and the cwd is what determines which plane a listener writes to, which is the property the election turns on anyway.

**3 — `.DS_Store` is a real blocklist gap** surfaced by the AC6 run. Not in scope here; noted so the OQ10b declaration work inherits it.

## Out of Scope

Making the OQ10 election · any mount/volume change · migrating any seat · the plane-identity AiConfig leaf (D#15595 lane-1 core, post-graduation) · mutating hydration behavior · fixing whatever drift the reconcile finds — **finding it is this ticket; fixing it is per-seat follow-up.**

## Avoided Traps

1. **Building a fresh inventory enumerator.** It becomes a second source of truth about the split, hand-maintained beside `DATA_SUBDIRS_BLOCKLIST` — the exact `DATA_SUBDIRS_TO_LINK` shape whose drift orphaned thousands of WAL records for 8 days.
2. **Reporting port *occupancy* instead of served identity.** `#15367`: a runner trusting any listener on a port executed a different checkout's tree, producing false greens as well as false reds. Occupancy is not identity.
3. **A falsifier satisfiable by explanation.** See the AC above — the reconcile must come back with residue or not; "I can explain that one" is not a pass.
4. **Treating this as the election.** It is the *input*. Nothing here decides bind-mount vs named-volume, and the ticket must not drift into deciding it.

## V-B-A: the load-bearing premise holds — `symlinkDataDir()` admits a non-mutating mode in three guards

The whole ticket rests on one assumption I asserted from the function's *return shape* rather than its *control flow*: that a non-mutating mode is a flag, not a rewrite. If the structure fought it — mutations interleaved with the classification — the reshape would be wrong and a fresh tool would be the honest answer after all. So I checked before writing anything.

**It holds.** Every mutation in `symlinkDataDir()`'s per-item loop is late and separable:

| Call | Kind |
|---|---|
| `fs.mkdir(parentDst, {recursive: true})` | mutation — parent `.neo-ai-data/` creation, once, before the loop |
| `fs.readdir` / `fs.lstat` / `fs.readlink` / `fs.realpath` ×2 | **pure reads** — these are the entire classification |
| `fs.rm(dst, …)` | mutation — clobber path, `force` only |
| `fs.symlink(src, dst, …)` | mutation — the link itself |

Everything that *decides* an item's class — blocklisted, already-linked, no-source, needs-clobber, linkable — is computed from reads **before** any of the three mutations, and the outcome is recorded via `result.<bucket>.push(name)` independently of whether the mutation then runs. The `alreadyLinked` and `skippedNoSource` branches already `continue` without mutating at all.

**So the non-mutating mode is:** skip the `mkdir`, guard `fs.rm` and `fs.symlink`, and record into the same buckets. The returned action map is **identical in shape** to the mutating run — which is what makes it a reconcile report rather than a second enumeration.

**One design consequence worth carrying into the PR:** the fail-closed throw on an unexpected symlink target (`:499`, *"Managed hydration never adopts another checkout's state implicitly"*) must **not** be suppressed in dry-run. A reconcile that swallows the divergence it exists to find would be worse than no reconcile. It stays a throw — or, better for a multi-seat sweep, becomes a recorded `divergent` bucket so one bad seat does not abort the run before the others are classified. **That bucket is exactly @neo-opus-grace's "unexplained residue"**, so the falsifier AC and the error path are the same object. I had them as separate concerns when I filed; they are not.

**Status:** PR still held behind #15781 / #15786 per the bench note. This V-B-A is the part that does not need a seat, and it changes the implementation shape (a fourth bucket, not just a flag), so it is worth recording before the code rather than discovering during review.

— Ada (@neo-opus-ada)

* feat(ai): reconcile mode for symlinkDataDir — classify without mutating (#15791)

Lane 1's early slice asked for a per-seat data-root inventory tool. Three
of its four axes already existed: symlinkDataDir enumerates every child
of canonical's .neo-ai-data against DATA_SUBDIRS_BLOCKLIST, realpaths
both sides, refuses foreign targets, and returns a per-item action map
that IS the inventory. Building a fresh enumerator would have created a
second source of truth about the split, hand-maintained beside the
blocklist — the retired DATA_SUBDIRS_TO_LINK shape whose drift orphaned
thousands of WAL records across clones for ~8 days.

So this is a mode, not a tool. dryRun skips the mkdir and guards the rm
and the symlink; every classification is computed from reads that already
ran before any write, so the decision is byte-identical to the mutating
pass and only the writes are withheld.

Two additions the V-B-A surfaced, both needed for the output to be
decision-grade for the data-root election rather than descriptive:

- `divergent` records what the mutating path throws on. A reconcile that
  aborts on the first deviant seat cannot classify the rest, and one that
  swallowed the divergence would be worse than none. The mutating path
  still refuses, unchanged — adopting another checkout's state silently
  is the failure, and recording is only safe because nothing is written.
- `blocklisted` + `resolved` make the map exhaustive. That is what lets
  the run assert no unexplained residue, replacing my weaker
  "explicable as provisioning-era drift" — which could be satisfied by
  constructing a story rather than taking a measurement.

The residue acceptance test and the error path turned out to be the same
object; I had filed them as separate concerns.

so they bind to this change rather than passing incidentally.

* feat(ai): probe host port claims by SERVED checkout, not occupancy (#15791)

The fourth axis of a per-seat data-root reconcile. Axes 1-3 are derived
from the hydration contract by symlinkDataDir dryRun; host port claims
have no declaration to derive from, so they must be observed.

Served identity rather than occupancy, because "port 8080 is busy" is
not the useful fact. A runner that trusted any listener on a port once
executed a different checkout's tree and produced false greens as well
as false reds. The question a multi-seat host has to answer is WHOSE
process is on the port, and the honest answer is the serving process's
working directory.

That also makes the probe a direct read of the property the data-root
election turns on: path leaves resolve relative to the invoking
process's cwd, so a listener's cwd IS the plane it writes to. Several
seats claiming adjacent ports from different checkouts is not a port
conflict; it is several planes wearing one host's port namespace.

Read-only by construction — lsof only, never connects to a port, never
sends a request, never signals. A fingerprint needing an HTTP round-trip
would make the diagnostic a client of the thing it diagnoses. Unknown is
reported rather than guessed when a process is not inspectable; a wrong
checkout attribution is worse than an absent one.

Parser split from the shell seam so the record-folding contract is
testable without a host that happens to have the right listeners
running. lsof -F pcn is stateful across lines, which is the part worth
pinning.

Live smoke on this host found several distinct checkouts serving ports
from one namespace — the finding the probe exists to surface, on first
run. Specific paths withheld here per critical-gate 9.

Test evidence: 8 passed, fixture-driven.

the falsifier hunts is exactly the kind canonical has no record of.
dryRun now enumerates the union and reports a seatOnly bucket.

The exhaustiveness claim was also wrong in the other direction: a
force-clobbered leaf appears in both clobbered and linked, so "exactly
one bucket" was false in the mutating path too. clobbered is not an
outcome — it records that a linked item displaced local data first.
Claim corrected, and the uniqueness test now runs over outcome buckets
with a force case pinning the overlap.

--reconcile wires the mode and emits ONE artifact combining both axes:
the declaration-derived plane classification and the observed port
claims. A caller that has to run two commands and staple the output
together is not a report, it is a suggestion.

The residue line states the observation, not a verdict. Non-zero residue
has at least two readings — an incomplete blocklist, or a seat never
hydrated with --link-data — and the report must not pick one. A
diagnostic that concludes is a diagnostic you have to re-derive.

First run on a live worktree: 10 linked, 3 blocklisted, 6 divergent
(all clone-local-non-symlink, including sqlite and wake-daemon), 7
distinct checkouts serving this host. The falsifier came back non-clean
on a real seat, which is what it exists to do.

Test evidence: 61 passed, +2 covering seat-only and force-clobber.

Co-Authored-By: Emmy <neo-gpt-emmy@neomjs.com>
Co-Authored-By: Euclid <neo-gpt@neomjs.com>

* fix(ai): a reconcile that cannot look must not report clean (#15791)

Four ways the reconcile said "clean" without having compared anything, plus the
executable boundary that makes the report reachable for a seat other than this one.

- FORCE-INVARIANT classification. `force` moved a clone-local leaf out of
  `divergent` into clobbered+linked, so the same seat with the same untouched
  file reported residue 1 without `--force` and residue 0 with it. A falsifier a
  mutation-intent flag can switch off is not a falsifier. `clobbered` is now a
  mutating-path-only bucket, which also makes the one-bucket property hold under
  dryRun without an exception to state.
- An ABSENT canonical is "could not compare", not "nothing to report". The ENOENT
  branch returned every bucket empty before the seat was ever enumerated, so a
  seat full of residue read as clean. Seat enumeration does not depend on
  canonical being readable and no longer waits for it.
- An UNREADABLE seat is not an empty one. Permissions hide exactly the leaves the
  falsifier exists to find; an absent seat dir is genuinely empty and still
  reports ok. `observed.{canonical,seat}` carries both facts and the CLI gates
  the word `(clean)` on them.
- Blocklisted children carry a `resolved` path. "We skipped it" is not an
  observation; a deliberately seat-local leaf makes WHERE it lives the one fact
  worth recording.

CLI:
- `--link-data --dry-run` routes to the read-only path. It was the obvious
  spelling and the dangerous one: `dryRun` reached prune mode only, so the safe-
  looking flag pair ran the full mutating bootstrap.
- `--seat <path>`, repeatable. `projectRoot` comes from the module's own
  directory, so not even changing cwd could retarget the reconcile — the
  multi-seat question needed both seats inside one process.
- Port claims sit once at the top of the report. Listeners are a property of the
  host; printing them under each seat implies a seat owns them.

The port probe reports `byCwd`/`servedCwds`, not checkouts. It never validates a
cwd as a repository root, so it must not name one — the cwd is what determines
which plane a listener writes to, which is the claim the measurement supports.

* fix(ai): a blocklisted leaf living only on the seat vanished from the report (#15791)

Fifth instance of this PR's one bug, and the worst-looking one: both sides
reported `observed: ok`, residue read 0, and the leaf was simply absent from
every bucket. Nothing looked wrong.

Cause: the seat-union pass skipped declared-local names outright, so only
canonical's children could ever populate `blocklisted`. A blocklisted child that
exists only on the seat is not an edge case — it is precisely what the blocklist
is for. Found by @neo-gpt-emmy; reproduced here before fixing.

The seat pass now yields to canonical only on shared names and classifies
everything else: declared-local → `blocklisted`, otherwise → `seatOnly`, both
with a `resolved` entry. `resolved` is now uniformly the realpath or `null`,
rather than falling back to the unresolved path in one branch and null in
another.

Test evidence, stated exactly: the seat-only-blocklisted regression fails against
unfixed source. The both-sides-classified-once test does NOT — old code could not
double-count because it skipped the name entirely. It guards the property the fix
could have broken on its way past, which is a different job from pinning the
defect, and is not a RED.

75 pass.

- 2026-07-24T20:47:51Z @tobiu referenced in commit `0d04182` - "feat(ai): re-runnable plane-placement census for the #15800 cost table (#15835) (#15836)

* feat(ai): re-runnable plane-placement census for the #15800 cost table (#15800)

The placement election's AC-1 requires cost rows filled from measurement with
cited provenance rather than estimates. I had produced those rows from ad-hoc
shell pipelines, which satisfies the letter and not the point: nobody else can
re-run them, so each row becomes an assertion the moment the host changes. This
lands the two measurements as a committed read-only script.

AXIS 1 - plane-opener census. A module counts when its EXECUTABLE code both
resolves a plane path and performs a filesystem operation. Comments are stripped
first via acorn's onComment ranges, and that is load-bearing rather than tidy: a
line-based match counted doc-comment MENTIONS of plane paths as code paths and
inflated the first measurement from 52 to 61 (~20%). `buildScripts` dropped out
entirely once stripped - it was a pure comment match.

  total 52 = 33 host-side runners + 15 in-server modules + 4 UNCLASSIFIED

Three buckets, not two, and that is the point of the script rather than a detail.
My own first measurement reported "in-server: 15" while a two-bucket split of the
same data gives 19, because four modules are neither clearly host-invoked nor
clearly server-loaded (`ai/graph/storage/SQLite.mjs` genuinely runs on both
sides). Folding those into whichever side tidies the total is exactly the
unstated-definition problem this census exists to replace - it is why the filed
"22 host-resident plane-openers" and my measured 33 cannot be compared until one
operationalization is agreed. So ambiguity is reported, never assigned.

AXIS 2 - seat containment. For each entry in a seat's plane, resolve it and ask
whether it stays inside that seat's own plane root. An entry resolving outside is
not contained by a bind-mount of that root: in a container it dangles unless the
canonical root is also mounted at the identical absolute host path. Measured on
five seats, 42 of 42 symlinked leaves escape, and ZERO dangle on the host - which
is precisely why the class is invisible until something is containerised.

Deliberately NOT duplicated: hydration-state classification. That is
`bootstrapWorktree --reconcile`'s job (#15791), and two answers to one question is
worse than one answer somebody has to go find.

Nine specs cover the two rules a naive implementation gets wrong invisibly: a
comment-only mention must not count (blanked, not deleted, so offsets survive);
an unparseable file is returned unchanged rather than silently dropped from a
census whose purpose is completeness; an escaping symlink counts as an escape
even though `existsSync` says it is fine; a symlink resolving inside the plane
does not; a seat with no plane reports absent rather than throwing; and the three
buckets must sum to the total with the prefix rules holding.

Read-only by construction: `git ls-files` + `readFileSync` + `lstat`/`realpath`.
No mkdir, no write, no symlink.

Refs #15800

* feat(ai): add per-seat WAL attribution as the census's third axis (#15835)

Folds the WAL-attribution measurement into the existing census rather than
opening a separate PR, because the queue is bounded by non-Claude review
capacity and a fifth Claude PR spends the scarce resource to no end.

The axis exists because @neo-opus-ada raised a per-seat precision cap on the
#15800 cost table: 29.7% of WAL bytes carried no agent field, framed as an
upstream write-path gap. Measured, that cap is a FIELD-NAME artifact, not a real
gap. `metadata.agent` is caller-supplied and optional (MemoryService.mjs:410,
`if (agent)`); `metadata.agentIdentity` is server-stamped from the bound identity
(:408). On a live day-segment `agent` was absent on 144/362 records while
`agentIdentity` was absent on ZERO. The loss was not uniform: `agent` erased two
seats outright and halved a third, so a cost row built on it would have priced the
plane as though two agents never wrote to it. Ada has since retracted the cap; this
lands the correction as a re-runnable instrument so it cannot re-fabricate.

The axis streams the newest day-segment, attributes by `agentIdentity`,
normalises the leading `@` so one seat cannot split into two rows, excludes the
derived `.graph`/`.embedded` projections, and ALWAYS reports the unattributed
bucket even at zero — omitting it quotes shares of a total it did not measure.
Live run: 367/367 records attributed, unattributed 0.0%.

Why the WAL axis belongs beside the other two: `memory-wal` is absent from the
hydration blocklist, so every hydrated seat's WAL directory resolves to the SAME
canonical directory by design (cross-clone sole-drainer enforcement), and segments
are day-keyed, so `du` on the directory cannot be disaggregated into seats at all.
Per-seat volume must come from the records, which is what this does.

Five new specs, 14 green. Red-proof: switching the read to `metadata.agent` turns
the field-distinction spec RED, attributing a record to the wrong caller label.

Refs #15800, #15835

* fix(ai): fix the census measurement contract per cross-family review (#15835)

Addresses @neo-gpt-emmy's CHANGES_REQUESTED on PR #15836. All four falsifiers
reproduced on the exact head before fixing.

1. THE CENSUS COUNTED ITSELF. Committed, the instrument matched its own opener
   rule and reported 53/34 where the body said 52/33 — the verifier moved the
   baseline it exists to reproduce. `listCensusFiles` now excludes its own path
   explicitly (CENSUS_SELF_PATH), stated rather than silently subtracted.

2. THE PLANE-PATH MATCHER SAW ONLY `storagePaths`. SwarmHeartbeatService reads
   `AiConfig.wakeDaemonHeartbeatAlivePath` and was missed, while `configBase.mjs`
   declares a whole family of plane leaves (backupPath, logPath, hierarchyPath,
   lazyEdgesQueuePath, handoffFilePath, dataPath, socketPath, ...). PLANE_PATH_SOURCE
   now recognises the `AiConfig.<name>Path|Dir` shape. This is a SHAPE proxy for
   the config contract, disclosed as such: a leaf not ending Path/Dir is still
   missed, and the durable fix (reconcile against the declared member set) stays
   scoped to the ticket rather than pretended. Net effect: 52 -> 70 openers, which
   is how badly the storagePaths-only rule was undercounting.

3. ESCAPE AND DANGLING WERE NOT ORTHOGONAL. The escape check derived its target
   from realpathSync, which throws on a dangling link and fell through to
   `continue` — so a link pointing OUTSIDE the root to a non-existent target
   counted as dangling only. Escape is now decided from the LITERAL target
   (readlinkSync), which exists whether or not the target resolves, and each
   escaped entry carries its own `dangling` flag.

4. THE JSDoc OVERSHOT WHAT THE CODE PROVES. It said an fs op is performed "on" the
   plane path; the regex proves only module-wide CO-OCCURRENCE (names a plane path
   AND calls fs somewhere), not data flow. Narrowed the claim to co-occurrence and
   named the consequence: a small over-count, which is the honest failure direction
   for a cost CEILING — it never under-reports the openers a branch must pay for.

Four new specs, 18 green. Red-proof, each isolated: reverting the self-exclusion
turns the self-count test RED; reverting escape-from-literal-target turns the
both-escaping-and-dangling test RED.

Not done here, scoped to #15835: deriving the plane-member set from the config
contract instead of a name shape, and the Contract Ledger for the CLI/output/
classification semantics. Both are authority-reconciliation work the reviewer
correctly flags as the durable fix; this closes the four exact-head falsifiers.

Refs #15835

* fix(ai): resolve containment per-condition, not lexical-only (#15835)

Cycle-2 fix from @neo-gpt-emmy's census review. My cycle-1 repair over-corrected:
to catch a dangling link's escape I switched escape resolution from realpathSync
to a purely LEXICAL path.resolve — which then MISSED chained escapes. A link whose
text reads inside the plane (`sub/x`) escapes anyway when an intermediate
component (`sub`) is itself a symlink pointing out, and only canonical resolution
follows that chain. I traded one correctness for another.

The two target identities answer different questions and neither substitutes:
lexical says "where does the link text point"; canonical says "where does this
existing entry actually resolve". So the choice is now PER CONDITION — canonical
(realpathSync) for a resolvable target, lexical (readlinkSync + resolve) only when
the target dangles and has no canonical form.

Red-proof: reverting to lexical-only drops `entry` from the escaped set on a
chained-escape fixture (link text inside, intermediate symlink out) — Received
["sub"], expected to contain "entry". The earlier escape-AND-dangling case still
passes, so the dangling path is not regressed.

19 green (18 + the chained-escape spec).
